title: Privacy-Enhancing Technologies Compared
description: Interactive SVG 2x2 comparison of four privacy-enhancing technologies (FHE, MPC, Differential Privacy, Zero-Knowledge Proofs) across definition, input/output visibility, computational cost, and maturity, with a real-world example tooltip per card.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity
chapter_title: Cryptography in Practice: PKI, TLS, and Data Protection

educational.topic: Privacy-enhancing technologies (FHE, MPC, differential privacy, zero-knowledge proofs)
learningObjectives: Compare four privacy-enhancing technologies across the same six fields.
Reason about who can see inputs and outputs under each technique.
Match each technique to the kind of privacy question it answers and its maturity.
educational.prerequisites: Basic cryptography (encryption, the idea of a ciphertext) and the notion of a trusted party.

pedagogical.modelType: static comparison cards with hover reveals
controls: Read the 2x2 grid of cards (FHE, MPC, DP, ZKP)
Compare the six fields across cards
Hover/tap a card for its real-world deployment example
Read the footer band on when to reach for which technique
pedagogical.assessment: Given a privacy requirement, students pick the appropriate technique and justify the choice using the input/output visibility and cost fields.
misconceptionsAddressed: Treating all privacy-enhancing technologies as interchangeable.
Assuming the most expensive technique (FHE) is always the most appropriate.
